text: We evaluated mixup between weak-labeled examples on the MultiRC testbed, averaging over num_seeds = 5 random seeds. The method achieves a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.17 with a standard error of 0.06, indicating that only a small fraction of the gap between the weak supervisor and the strong ceiling is recovered by this interpolation scheme. Because no baseline PGR was supplied in the provided data, we cannot characterize this number as an improvement over any comparison method, nor can we assess whether the measured value exceeds an alternative by a margin that the seed count would support. The standard error is sizeable relative to the point estimate, so the underlying per-seed spread is non-trivial and the interval around 0.17 should be treated as wide. We therefore report the result descriptively: mixup on weak labels yields a modest, uncertain PGR on MultiRC, and additional seeds plus an explicit baseline would be needed before drawing comparative conclusions.
